caption: The drawing features a technical illustration of a four-poster canopy bed, presented in both side elevation and top-down plan views. The bed is constructed with four prominent, straight posts at the corners connected by horizontal beams at the head, foot, and top, and includes two curtains drawn to the sides illustrated by curved lines. The side view on the lower half shows the head of the bed to the left with a sloped pillow and mattress indicated in gray shading, while the right section shows an empty frame with a partial curtain extending downward, and dimensions are specified in inches (for example, 57 1/2”, 73”, and 17 1/2” between major sections). The top section contains a rectangle depicting the plan of the mattress support with a grid pattern of red and gray lines labeled as “ROPE SPRING.” Annotations at the top right note details about “BLISS HOUSE - SPRINGFIELD, MASS. -- BUILT 1750 - MAPLE - NEW ENGLAND TYPE: 1700-1780,” and the scale is given as “1/4”=1’.” The name “JACK BOCHNER” and “BKLN MUSEUM” are also written near the top right. The entire drawing is rendered in fine black ink with red highlights, especially on the rope spring grid and under-frame, and is presented on a cream background.
title: Bed
